summary: Practise QGIS access mapping, city indicators, and evidence-based planning briefs in a 5-day foundation course. Explore the course.
lede: Data-driven urban planning uses service, transport, and location data to assess needs and inform planning decisions. For urban planners, transport analysts, and municipal service teams, the course develops practical skills in checking data quality, calculating comparable indicators, and mapping service access with QGIS. It also introduces transport-coverage analysis and ways to document assumptions and uncertainty when presenting evidence for priorities.
audienceIntro: This smart cities course is designed for people who turn urban service and location data into planning evidence.
modules: ISO 37120 Foundations for Smart Cities Data Analytics
Spreadsheets for Smart Cities Data Quality
QGIS Access Mapping for Smart Cities
GTFS Transport Coverage for Smart Cities
QGIS Service Prioritization for Smart Cities
OpenStreetMap Context for Smart Cities Planning
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with spreadsheets and simple charts will help you complete the indicator exercises. No coding or programming is required.
topics: Statistics & data analysis (SPSS, Stata, R, Python)
